samples.identification: Gutem Jekyll personal blog source archive
samples.reason: The repository is a Jekyll blog with Portuguese malware research articles and an unreferenced .sample research specimen. The workflow builds Jekyll, generates images from Markdown titles, indexes the rendered site and deploys it. Neither the workflow nor first-party tooling invokes the specimen. Its attack code remains dangerous if deliberately run; that content does not make this research archive an active stealer package.
reverse_engineering: Decoded the shell python -c command, its Base64 exec wrapper, the full embedded collection script, and PERSIST_B64 without running payload code.

emit opens regular files and writes their contents to stdout. Targets include SSH private keys, AWS/GCP/Azure and Kubernetes credentials, .env/configuration files, wallet key material, shell histories and /etc/shadow. run captures host/user/network commands and environment variables.

The wrapper feeds collected code to a child Python interpreter on stdin, captures stdout to a temporary file, generates an OpenSSL session key, AES-256-CBC/PBKDF2 encrypts the collected file, RSA-OAEP wraps the session key, tars both encrypted files and curl POSTs the archive to models.litellm.cloud.

The in-cluster branch uses the serviceaccount bearer token to list Kubernetes secrets/namespaces/nodes. It constructs and POSTs a privileged hostPID/hostNetwork pod for each node, mounting host / at /host and attempting to write/enable a Python systemd agent through chroot.

The agent sleeps 300 seconds, reads a URL from checkmarx.zone/raw, downloads changed non-YouTube results, chmods the path, launches it in a new session with discarded output, saves the URL and polls after 3000 seconds.

The blog article quotes parts of these paths. Another article quotes GitHub Actions secrets exported to webhook.site, dependency package tampering and worm behavior; an import and a webhook URL in those listings do not establish OS-profile exfiltration.

Site JavaScript implements footnote and table-of-contents UI. Production templates load Google Tag Manager/web-vitals and OneSignal; the service worker imports the OneSignal SDK. Preserve their communications and execution observations. Sass cache files have ordinary Sass::Tree cache structure, not an invoked payload entry point.
limits: Success of collection/export depends on permissions, installed openssl/tar/curl and endpoint availability; no success or compromise of the analysis machine was observed.

AWS calls are attempts, not demonstrated secret extraction: ListSecrets uses an invalid JSON-shaped request body, GetSecretValue lacks SecretId and its result is unused, and SSM uses a mismatched request format.

PERSIST_B64 is assigned only inside the serviceaccount branch. Local fallback without that branch catches NameError after creating an empty file. Kubernetes service installation writes a user-unit path but invokes system systemctl enable; effective node persistence is not established.
No evidence of deliberate sample execution on a found machine is supplied. That deployment fact would matter; the supplied packaging instead establishes a research site.

samples.reason: An otherwise ordinary Gentoo build recipe starts with executable rm -rf /* at global shell scope. Sourcing it attempts recursive deletion of root children with the invoking user privileges, before any build function. This destructive action contradicts speech-recognition training installation and is sufficient evidence without external reputation.
reverse_engineering: Line 1 is rm -rf /*, a real shell command rather than a quote/comment/heredoc. Expansion selects root children and bypasses the rm safeguard against an operand exactly equal to /. It does not imply all deletions will succeed.

Remaining metadata and src_install/pkg_postinst are a conventional Gentoo speech-training recipe with SourceForge source, dependencies, documentation installation and Python shebang/bytecode processing.
The three hostile rules cover the root wipe and the destructive package-recipe context. They overlap around one destructive primitive; no extra hostile actions were invented to satisfy a trait count.
limits: Deletion reach depends on the account/filesystem protections; no machine-deployment or runtime-success evidence is supplied. Intentional root deletion is established statically.

samples.reason: The application entry routine calls browser password/cookie extraction, wallet directory copying and Discord token harvesting; tokens and staged files are sent to a configured webhook/file host. Multi-layer concealment, sandbox exits and console hiding corroborate theft. The artifact is damaged source rather than a working benign application; its parse/configuration failures do not erase the attack implementation.
reverse_engineering: Inspected and evaluated only pure decoder functions/literal table builders in QuickJS with no host APIs exposed, a time limit and memory limit. Recovered the LZW table, basE91 table, arithmetic string-array rotation and aliases; never invoked the application.

Entry waits for connectivity, creates the stealer context, sets the process title to Installer, checks VM artifacts/blacklisted user-domain-host names, creates an HTTPS agent with rejectUnauthorized: ![], hides the console, closes browsers and starts collection.

Browser routines query Chromium login/cookie stores, use os_crypt/encrypted_key plus Windows DPAPI unprotectData and AES-GCM decryption, and stage plaintext records. Session-cookie routines query social-service account data and send cookie/account embeds.

Discord collection enumerates LevelDB log/ldb files across Discord/browser profiles, extracts plaintext/encrypted tokens, obtains the key through DPAPI, decrypts AES-GCM tokens, validates them against Discord APIs and sends account/token embeds to the configured webhook.

Wallet collection enumerates configured wallet directories and copies them into a staging tree. ZIP creation and GoFile/webhook upload routines export collected files; the main routine later deletes staging files.

Discord-core modification fetches a template, substitutes webhook placeholders and writes it into located desktop_core entry files when its collection helper is invoked. A separate token-protector bypass routine rewrites protection options, but an invocation was not established.

A method called add_to_startup copies argv0 to Start Menu/Updater.exe and renames the same path. This is not the Startup folder and proves no logon activation. A clipper call is wrapped in try/catch and utils.clipper is not initialized; do not infer an operating clipboard stealer from it.
limits: The original ends with an incomplete JSON fragment after the bundle, which prevents parsing. Its first env assignment has no supplied binding, and config_obf.js/config.js are absent. No working deployment or successful theft is claimed.

The raw scanner does not fully reconstruct the LZW/basE91 and rotated string tables; flow analysis reports limitations. YAML-only weak word rules were not added to pretend that this reconstruction gap is solved.

coverage_result: No existing batch observation was lost after canonical ID mapping. The archive changes from 12 hostile/14 suspicious to 10 hostile/11 suspicious by retaining overclaimed evidence as notable; the ebuild keeps 3 hostile/3 suspicious and JavaScript keeps 2 hostile/6 suspicious. Console hiding adds a notable call. Accurate embedded-malware signatures remain.

retained: Named consumers follow all relocated IDs.
Browser/profile/passkey source-specific consumers explicitly retain the encoded file-upload capability.
The two execution/DNS/whoami consumers retain the old endpoint/import observation as one alternative beside the existing OOB selector.

The Terraform credentials matcher moved from the cross-family credential leaf to secret-config; its two source-path consumers retain the same matcher. This makes room in the 100-rule credential leaf by correcting a pre-existing specific-path placement, not by splitting on capacity.
consumer_review.intentionally_not_restored: A generic API name, header helper, encoded directory, webhook identifier or endpoint/import co-occurrence is not itself credential theft or exfiltration. Broad theft/exfiltration ancestor selectors no longer inherit those overclaims. Their neutral facts remain available. New destination ancestor matches are type-disjoint from PE profiles or are the common fs ancestor already selecting the moved path.

tests.external_controls: The existing postinstall-oob-beacon.tgz and pypi-driftwoodmesh-import-oob-beacon-linux.whl were read as data and retain suspicious/hostile attack observations; the existing positive and full-lifecycle SDK source controls preserve inventory matching boundaries.

classifier_disagreements: The benign research archive remains ML-flagged (probability 0.99, level 25). Malicious embedded code detections were retained rather than suppressed to force a benign score.
The malicious ebuild remains outside the calibrated ML grid (0.9830746, level -1), despite 3 hostile rules.
